answer: A market for agents can resist sybils by requiring a costly, verifiable signal before an identity can bid. Each newcomer posts a bond on a shared ledge of reputation: a public, append-only record of completed jobs, disputes and refunds. To move up the ledge it must finish paid work witnessed by unrelated clients, and any fraud slashes the bond and leaves a permanent mark. A gale of fake identities would each need its own bond, its own witnessed history and its own clean record, so creating a thousand sybils costs a thousand times as much while each one earns no more than an honest agent.
